item.title: Panda-monium: When diplomacy goes to the dogs, horses, and elephants
item.description: Get ready, Atlanta! Two charming giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be gracing the zoo with their presence this Monday, thanks to a decade-long conservation agreement. This unique event reflects the tradition of panda diplomacy, which has played a pivotal role in fostering international friendships. The nuances of this approach reveal essential lessons in both diplomacy and environmental conservation.

item.title: New Green Card rules from September: Categories affected and those exempt
item.description: Beginning in September 2026, the USCIS unveiled new regulations affecting Green Card seekers. These guidelines emphasize the financial self-sufficiency of applicants while excluding those in humanitarian categories. Nearly all applicants, including family and various occupational groups, must satisfy these criteria. While the Form I-864, Affidavit of Support, is crucial, it cannot guarantee approval on its own.

item.title: $17.1M to restore 206,000 acres, 225 miles for wildlife movement in West
item.description: The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation has announced $13.3 million in grants for 14 projects across the western US. With $3.8 million in matching contributions, the conservation work will have a total impact of $17.1 million. The projects will restore habitat, improve migration corridors and modify 225 miles of fencing for wildlife.

item.title: California buried 662,700 tires under I-880 ramp, saved $477K, 22 years
item.description: Engineers faced challenges while upgrading a highway interchange in Milpitas due to unstable bay mud. They opted to use shredded waste tires as lightweight fill to prevent ground settlement. This choice reduced weight on the soft soil by 40 percent and saved significant project costs. Over two decades, the infrastructure has shown no maintenance issues or structural damage.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Playing reef sounds underwater attracted 14x more baby fish in Hawai'i test
item.description: In an exciting breakthrough, scientists discovered that playing sounds from thriving coral reefs significantly draws in young fish larvae. The study conducted in Kāne‘ohe Bay revealed an uptick in larval presence at sites featuring these sound recordings. However, the increased attraction was transient. This pioneering research indicates that using natural soundscapes might support reef restoration efforts, highlighting the need for further investigation into the lasting impacts on fish populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Florida used robot rabbits to hunt Burmese pythons threatening the Everglades
item.description: Florida is testing solar-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons in the Everglades. Developed by the South Florida Water Management District and University of Florida, the robotic decoys mimic prey using heat and scent while AI cameras detect approaching snakes. Officials can then alert trained removal agents, adding technology to Florida’s wider python control efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Rob Lowe says he was happy after Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at Oscars
item.description: Rob Lowe has revealed he was “the only person happy” when Will Smith slapped Chris Rock at the 2022 Oscars, hoping the shocking incident would overshadow his infamous 1989 Academy Awards performance. Lowe joked that his decades-old Oscars blunder continues to haunt him, despite Smith’s slap becoming one of Hollywood’s biggest controversies.

item.title: Jason and Kylie Kelce’s investment reaches 5,000 stores in $2.9 billion move
item.description: Jason Kelce has made a savvy equity investment in Hank Sauce via Winnie Capital, marking a significant step for both him and the brand. Once a local staple, Hank Sauce now boasts distribution in over 5,000 stores across the country. With a U.S. hot sauce market worth nearly $2.9 billion, this partnership looks to amplify Hank Sauce's visibility and reach nationally, taking advantage of the substantial growth opportunities ahead.

item.title: Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million Dodgers contract and what it means for MLB
item.description: Shohei Ohtani’s $700 million contract with the Los Angeles Dodgers sounds like a blockbuster headline figure, but the deal is far more unusual than that. The deal shifted the Dodgers' payroll strategy with $680 million deferred until 2034-43, and Ohtani's commercial appeal drew major attention in Japan and around the world. The deal also helped to change how massive player contracts can be structured by MLB teams.

item.title: 3 killed, 4 injured after fight erupts into gunfire at Detroit strip club in US
item.description: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.

item.title: 15,000 runs for Kohli! Virat joins Sachin Tendulkar in ODI record book
item.description: Virat Kohli reached 15,002 runs from 315 matches and 303 innings. He has scored 54 centuries and 80 fifties in ODIs, with a highest score of 183. His ODI batting average stands at 58.83, while his strike rate is more than 94.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Parvesh Verma slap row: Man files complaint, police reveal prior FIR against him
item.description: Delhi Police has received a complaint regarding an alleged incident involving Minister Parvesh Verma. The complaint states that Verma slapped a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. AAP leader Jarnail Singh was present and questioned the quality of the road when the incident occurred. Verma disputes the allegations, claiming the video does not show the full context.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Are Justin and Patrick Herbert brothers? The Oregon and Chargers connection explained
item.description: In a thrilling matchup against the Buffalo Bills, Patrick Herbert prepares for his NFL debut, teaming up with his brother Justin Herbert. The duo, who played together at Oregon, never connected on any passes during their college years. After going undrafted in 2025, Patrick joined the Chargers' practice squad, and following tight end injuries, he's been promoted to the active roster.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: ‘Illegal detention by Assam Police has finally ended’: CJP’s Ranka to address press
item.description: Ashutosh Ranka, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janta Party, reported his detention by Assam Police has ended. He stated that he will address the media after being taken back to the original pick-up location. Several other CJP leaders were also detained in Guwahati before a regional volunteers' meeting near the Assam Secretariat. Police prevented access to the meeting site, which aimed to gather around 200-300 volunteers from the region.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: 'Won't bow our head': Iran embassy invokes Baahubali to echo Pezeshkian's UN speech
item.description: Highlighting the parallels between resilience and heroism, the Iranian Embassy in Hyderabad unveiled a video featuring President Masoud Pezeshkian's UNGA address likened to the epic tale of Baahubali. The embassy conveyed Iran's steadfastness against external pressures, as exemplified in Dr. Pezeshkian's rejection of U.S. sanctions. He asserted Iran's commitment to dialogue while maintaining a robust defense posture, amidst escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: 'I promised myself': Virat Kohli after 15,000-run landmark
item.description: Virat Kohli became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to complete 15,000 ODI runs. He also hit his record-extending 55th ODI century as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the first ODI. Kohli said his priority has always been to understand the situation and do what the team needs.
item.dc:creator: AMIT KUMAR

item.title: Asian Games: Athletics leads India’s seven-medal haul, three boxers assure medals
item.description: India showcased a stellar performance at the Asian Games 2026, clinching a total of seven medals, predominantly in athletics and squash. Parul Chaudhary shone brightly, securing a bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase. Silver medals were added by Ancy Sojan and Sarvesh Kushare in their respective disciplines. The boxing team also excelled, confirming three medals through successful semifinal performances.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
item.description: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: IndiGo A321 enroute Blr suffers tail strike; plane lands safely in second attempt
item.description: On Sunday, an IndiGo Airbus A321 operating flight 6E 6542 experienced a tail strike during a go-around. The incident occurred while attempting to land in gusty weather at Bengaluru airport. All passengers and crew were safely disembarked, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and has engaged with IndiGo regarding pilot training enhancements.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH SINHA

item.title: US rejects Iran's claim of capturing underwater drone, calls move 'desperate'
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reported the capture of a US underwater drone in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. In response, the US military dismissed this assertion, clarifying that the drone in question had experienced a malfunction prior to any claims from Iran. This development follows Iran's earlier announcement regarding another US military drone capture.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: '40km chase': Cop clings to speeding car to catch smugglers in Coimbatore; watch
item.description: In Coimbatore district, Kovilpalayam police engaged in a thrilling 40km chase after suspected smugglers failed to heed police signals. Remarkably, a daring officer climbed onto the suspects' vehicle during the pursuit, making it a high-stakes operation. The pursuit came to an end when the police successfully intercepted the fleeing car, leading to the suspects' arrest. However, details about the smuggling operation are still scarce.
item.dc:creator: TYSION PRABHU

item.title: Virat Kohli breaks Sachin Tendulkar's record for most ODI centuries against a team
item.description: The century was Virat Kohli's 55th in ODI cricket. It was also his 86th international hundred. His international centuries include 30 in Tests, 55 in ODIs and one in T20Is. Kohli has now scored 55 ODI hundreds, extending his lead among active players in the format.

item.title: France steps in to protect Saudi oil infrastructure as Houthi attacks intensify
item.description: France's military support to Saudi Arabia will involve deploying troops and defense systems to protect key energy infrastructure. The deployment follows repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities and aims to secure the Red Sea port of Yanbu. French official Jean-Noel Barrot emphasized that France's role is strictly defensive and does not equate to participation in the conflict.

item.title: CJP says Mumbai Police denied Oct 2 protest permission, launches 'Jail Bharo Andolan'
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party is gearing up for a protest in Mumbai after being denied police permission. Founder Abhijeet Dipke announced plans for a Jail Bharo Andolan on Gandhi Jayanti. This announcement follows reports of CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka and volunteers facing detention in Assam. NCP (SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande condemned the detentions, labeling them illegal and unconstitutional. The CJP remains dedicated to advocating for social issues despite these setbacks.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Asian Games: Why India dropped out of top 10 despite winning seven more medals
item.description: India added seven medals on Day 8 of the Asian Games, including two silver medals in squash and five in athletics. Parul Chaudhary achieved a new national record in the women's 3000m steeplechase, winning bronze. However, India did not win any gold medals, leading to a drop in its overall standings. Boxers Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, and Narender secured medals by reaching the semifinals.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: IIT-B student suicide: What law says about abetment, instigation and ‘guilty mind’
item.description: The heartbreaking suicide of a second-year IIT-Bombay student has ignited debates over complex legal matters concerning abetment. Professor Suryanarayana Doolla finds himself charged with abetting the tragedy, drawing emotional protests from the victim's family. The rarity of successful prosecutions in such cases poses additional challenges, as the Supreme Court insists on clear evidence of intentional instigation.
item.dc:creator: SWATI DESHPANDE AND REBECCA SAMERVEL

item.title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
item.description: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Critics, including numerous political leaders, argued that such an action would jeopardize transparency and obstruct public access to crucial law records. In response to widespread criticism, the government promptly withdrew the exemption, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the RTI Act.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN
